- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, reduce forecasted price momentum; model tends to overreact to negative sentiment.  
- If sentiment spikes above 0.7 and price rises sharply, model often over-forecasts later peaks — cap forecasted peaks at +10% above recent high.  
- When true price diverges >5% from forecast in early days of 30d window, adjust later days downward if sentiment remains neutral or negative.  
- Model tends to underestimate late-period price surges (last 5–7 days of 30d) — especially if sentiment is positive and rising.  
- If forecast shows early “overshoot” (e.g., first 3–5 days > true price), apply a 2–3 day lag correction: subtract 0.5–1.0 from forecasted values starting from day 6.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecasted price is >15% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- Sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating 0.2–0.8) suggests model should smooth forecasts — avoid sharp directional changes unless sentiment confirms trend.
